metas.name: Apurimac Abancay Town
metas.note: The town of Abancay is surrounded by tall, brown mountains with sparse vegetation, visible from most parts of the city.

metas.name: Apurimac Gen 3 Landscape
metas.note: The gen 3 coverage near Andahuaylas is tricky. The landscape looks lush, similar to Cajamarca. The combination of very overcast skies, black gen 3 car, and tall eucalyptus trees is a good clue for this area.

metas.name: Arequipa Town
metas.note: Arequipa has a distinctive colonial-style architecture, with arched windows and small overhanging roofs. Many houses in the old-town are built from sillar, a white volcanic rock. This cobblestone pavement is also quite common in the city.

metas.name: Cajamarca Town
metas.note: Cajamarca city can be identified by its abundance of northern-style roofs (overhanging with wooden supports) and white colonial-style architecture.

metas.name: Cusco City
metas.note: The town of Cusco has both red brick houses and white Spanish colonial-style buildings. It is surrounded by mountains. Buildings with orange or red tiled roofs are most common in Cusco region.

metas.name: Huanuco Town
metas.note: The city of Huanuco is surrounded by huge dark-green, barren mountains.

metas.name: Junin Huancayo
metas.note: Huancayo can be recognized by the huge mountains surrounding the city, as well as its grid.

metas.name: Lima Town
metas.note: A good clue for Lima is overcast weather, as other coastal areas often have clear blue skies. Boulevard-type streets are also mostly only found in Lima.

metas.name: Loreto Iquitos Town
metas.note: Roads inside Iquitos have both the dark asphalt found on the road to Iquitos and concrete pavement. Transitions between these pavement types are often in poor condition.

metas.name: Moquegua Ilo
metas.note: Moquegua’s second-largest city, Ilo, is a somewhat hilly coastal city surrounded by sand dunes.

metas.name: Moquegua Mountains
metas.note: The city of Moquegua is surrounded by rocky, light-colored, dry mountains. These mountains are also a good way to recognize Moquegua region.

metas.name: Pasco Cerro de Pasco
metas.note: Cerro de Pasco is a very high-elevation mining town. The buildings have metal sheet roofs, and the town is surrounded by rugged, barren mountains.

metas.name: Pasco Oxapampa
metas.note: Oxapampa features wooden elements reminiscent of architecture in the Alps (this type of architecture can only be found in Pasco and Junin). The town can also be recognized by the forested, tropical hills that surround it.

metas.name: Piura Town
metas.note: The towns of Piura and Sullana can most easily be recognized by the abbundance of these mesquite trees, which are less common in coastal regions south of it.

metas.name: Puno Juliaca
metas.note: Juliaca is the largest town in the region and is flat, with a lot of red brick architecture. On gen 3 many of the roads inside the city are unpaved.

metas.name: San Martin Tarapoto Town
metas.note: Tarapoto is the largest city in the region. It is mostly gen 4 and somewhat hilly. If you are in a large tropical city with visible mountains, it’s likely Tarapoto.

metas.name: Tacna Sand Dunes
metas.note: Tacna is flanked by huge sand dunes on both sides of the city.

metas.name: Ucayali Pucallpa Gen 4
metas.note: The center of Pucallpa is gen 4. It is flat and well-paved. Check Pucallpa’s grid to verify. A similar-looking city is Yurimaguas, north of Tarapoto.
